title: tests/userspace/test_concurrent.c: 16-thread concurrent /dev/crypto2dev stress
description:
Concurrent stress test for /dev/wolfcrypt streaming interface.

Design: 16 threads, each opens its own fd (one fd = one session). No shared fds.

Per-thread loop (10,000 iterations):
1. open('/dev/wolfcrypt', O_RDWR)
2. WOLFKM_IOC_INIT with AES-CBC-256 encrypt, random key
3. WOLFKM_IOC_SET_IV with random IV
4. write() 4096 bytes of random plaintext
5. read() 4096 bytes ciphertext
6. close() — verifies key zeroization (no crashes on concurrent close)
7. Repeat with AES-GCM and SHA-256 on alternating iterations

Verification: no crashes, no -EBADMSG false positives, no fd state leakage between iterations (open a new fd each time).

Also test: two threads sharing the same fd must not corrupt each other's in-flight data (write/read must be serialized per-fd by the spinlock in wolfkm_fd_state).
design: Each thread: open(/dev/wolfcrypt), SESSION_NEW x3, loop 10000 times (CRYPT each session), SESSION_FREE x3, close. Use pthread_barrier_t to start all threads simultaneously. Verify results by round-trip (encrypt then decrypt, compare to original). Report total_ops/sec at end. Any error is a test failure.
acceptance_criteria: 16 threads × 10,000 ops completes without deadlock, crash, or incorrect results. No kernel BUG or Oops in dmesg. Throughput reported to stdout.
